vocab.definition: metals listed from most to least reactive.
a more reactive metal pushes out a less reactive one.
loss of electrons (metal forming an ion).
an unreactive metal found as the element, e.g. gold.

misconceptions.wrong: Gold is reactive because it is valuable.
misconceptions.right: Gold is very unreactive — that's why it stays shiny.
Only reactive metals react with cold water.

misconceptions.wrong: A less reactive metal displaces a more reactive one.
misconceptions.right: Only a MORE reactive metal can displace another.

questions.text: Put these in order of reactivity (most first): copper, potassium, zinc. [1 mark]

questions.text: Explain why magnesium fizzes faster than zinc in acid. [2 marks]

questions.text: Write the equation for zinc displacing copper from CuSO₄. [2 marks]

footer.tip: More reactive metals lose electrons more easily to form positive ions.
